items.raw_excerpt: The Ministry of Agriculture (MOA) on Tuesday touted a "Taiwan Peanut" label and elemental analysis to help locally grown peanuts compete against imports.

items.raw_excerpt: The first light rail transit (LRT) line on Phu Quoc Island that will cut travel time between the airport and the APEC to 20 minutes showcased architectural elements inspired by Vietnam’s three major regions along its six stations.
items.summary_en: Phu Quoc Island, Vietnam's largest island, is getting its first light rail transit line. The LRT will cut travel time between the airport and the APEC area to about 20 minutes. Its six stations showcase architectural elements inspired by Vietnam's three major regions.

items.raw_excerpt: Applicants for ancestry-based Italian citizenship blocked by a 1912 law will have a chance to have their case reviewed, under new guidance based on a ruling from Italy’s highest court.
items.summary_en: People who apply for Italian citizenship through their ancestors can now have their cases reviewed again. A 1912 law had blocked some applicants, but Italy's highest court made a new ruling. The new guidance gives these families another chance to become Italian citizens.
items.summary_ko: 조상을 통해 이탈리아 시민권을 신청하는 사람들이 이제 사건을 다시 검토받을 수 있게 되었습니다. 1912년 법률이 일부 신청자를 막았지만, 이탈리아 최고재판소가 새로운 판결을 내렸습니다. 새로운 지침으로 이 가족들에게 이탈리아 시민권을 얻을 다시 한번 기회가 주어집니다.

items.raw_excerpt: If your child is starting kindergarten this year or you are planning for the future, it’s important to know how to pay for this essential early childhood service in Norway.
items.summary_en: Norway offers ways for families to cut the cost of kindergarten. Parents can apply for subsidies and income-based discounts. The system helps make early childhood education affordable for all families.

items.raw_excerpt: Amsterdam cold case police are appealing for help identifying a man known as “Lucky” who collapsed on the street three years ago after suffering a suspected brain haemorrhage or stroke. Doctors believe he subsequently developed aphasia, which makes communication nearly impossible. No one has been able to work out who he is or where he came from. He now lives in a care home in Amsterdam Zuidoost and the only words he still uses are English ones – “nonsense” and...
items.summary_en: Amsterdam police are asking the public to help identify a man known only as Lucky. He collapsed on the street three years ago from a brain haemorrhage and now cannot speak except for two English words. He lives in a care home and no one knows who he is or where he came from.

items.raw_excerpt: More than 500 people have joined a campaign to stop a huge data centre being built in Amsterdam-Zuid, arguing that it will bring “zero benefits to the area”. The Dutch government has introduced restrictions on the size of data centres in recent years following criticism from provincial and municipal governments about the strain on the electricity network. Data centres accounted for 4.6% of all electricity use in the Netherlands in 2024. But the plans to build a 24,000 m2 facility...
items.summary_en: More than 500 people have joined a campaign to stop a huge data centre being built in Amsterdam-Zuid. The Dutch government has introduced restrictions on data centres due to strain on the electricity network. Residents say the 24,000 square metre facility will bring zero benefits to the area.

items.raw_excerpt: Plant-based foods now cost less than meat and dairy equivalents at nine major supermarkets in the Netherlands, according to new research published by food organisation ProVeg. “It’s remarkable that this is happening,” Martine van Haperen, nutrition and health expert at ProVeg, told DutchNews. “It’s normally been very difficult for plant-based products to compete with animal-based ones. What we’re seeing now is that store brands like Albert Heijn have expanded their own-brand products, making the
items.summary_en: Nine major supermarkets in the Netherlands now sell plant-based foods at lower prices than meat and dairy equivalents. Research from food organisation ProVeg found that store brands like Albert Heijn have expanded their plant-based product lines. This marks a shift as plant-based products have historically struggled to compete with animal-based ones on price.
